![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14143817/assets/99e3b108c8ba207b2890c4d0693c152930d9724dc084fb53b46d5cffba9d0804.svg)
question.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14143817/assets/6b6f467a3b456421d1cf5483dd88f410881e082f8f7490bc7a1a559f0befa8b1.svg)

The matrix $B^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14143817/assets/e7bea980fcdd14d3686b985c70eff7dd980952515dc856377ae8c1018cff0c38.svg)
